description:
Databricks SQL runs of ClickBench differ from BigQuery and Snowflake on two of 43 queries: Q43 at every scale, Q29 at SF 1 and SF 10 (at SF 0.1 all three return 0 rows for Q29, but the Databricks translation is wrong there too). BigQuery and Snowflake agree with each other on all 43.

- Q29: Databricks returns 0 rows at SF 0.1 and 1 row at SF 1 and SF 10; BigQuery and Snowflake return 0, 0 and 6. Cause confirmed: the Databricks translation keeps the `\1` backreference in `REGEXP_REPLACE(Referer, '^https?://(?:www\.)?([^/]+)/.*$', '\1')`, but Spark SQL needs `$1`, so every referrer collapses into one group.
- Q43: Databricks returns 1 row at every scale; BigQuery and Snowflake return 2, 22 and 159. The query groups by `DATE_TRUNC('MINUTE', EventTime)`. The Databricks DDL declares `EventTime TIMESTAMP NOT NULL`. Cause not yet identified; check how EventTime values are loaded on Databricks (type, parsing, time zone) and how DATE_TRUNC is translated.

The September 2026 Databricks ClickBench runs show the same counts, so this predates the cache-off reruns. The validator cannot detect it because ClickBench has no expected answers.

REVIEWED 2026-10-25 (TodoReview) against origin/develop 9a184b619 and fork main ea44bcc9 (30.24.0.13). VERIFIED FACTS (2026-10-25)
- Row counts recomputed from the published bundles (non-warmup measurement rows): Q29 Databricks 0/1/1 at SF0.1/1/10 vs BigQuery and Snowflake 0/0/6; Q43 Databricks 1/1/1 vs 2/22/159. The other 41 queries agree with DuckDB's counts on SF1 (Databricks matches 41 of 43 at SF1).
- Q29 cause is already documented as a known gap in the fork: downstream/ENGINE-GAPS.md says 'Spark and Databricks read `\1` in a replacement as the digit 1 (they expect `$1`); that is not changed by this slice.' The source text is in benchbox/core/clickbench/queries.py (`REGEXP_REPLACE(Referer, '^https?://(?:www\\.)?([^/]+)/.*$', '\\1')`). The fix therefore belongs in the fork (Spark/Databricks generator rewriting `\N` to `$N` in REGEXP_REPLACE replacements), with pyspark in fork CI as the executable engine.
- ROW COUNTS ARE A WEAK ORACLE HERE: at SF0.1 and SF1 the correct engines return 0 rows for Q29 (HAVING COUNT(*) > 100000), so the fix cannot be shown by row count below SF10; compare the grouped key values on a purpose-built dataset, and use SF10 (6 rows) for the end-to-end check.
- Q43: `SELECT DATE_TRUNC('minute', EventTime) ... WHERE CounterID = 62 AND EventDate >= '2013-07-14' AND EventDate <= '2013-07-15' AND IsRefresh = 0 AND DontCountHits = 0 GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('minute', EventTime) ORDER BY ...`; Databricks returns 1 group at every scale. Cause unidentified: candidates to test locally first are EventTime/EventDate load typing and time zone on the Databricks path and the DATE_TRUNC translation.
- The three bundles ran on a serverless 2X-Small Photon warehouse with validated cache-off receipts; total run durations 89.7 s (SF0.1), 193.3 s (SF1), 255.3 s (SF10); no cost_usd is recorded in the bundles, so a spend estimate must be supplied by the owner/Databricks billing, not inferred.
